summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted due to a subtherapeutic INR of 1.4 while on chronic warfarin therapy for a mechanical aortic valve. The cause was likely missed doses due to medication confusion. He was started on a heparin drip and resumed his home warfarin regimen. His INR rose to 2.1 within 24 hours and reached 2.4 by discharge, allowing safe discontinuation of heparin. His comorbidities, including diabetes, COPD, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and chronic diastolic heart failure, remained stable throughout the admission. A groin rash was diagnosed as fungal and treated with clotrimazole cream. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all medications, monitor INR the following day, and follow up with his PCP and anticoagulation clinic.
